Welcome to WHCP

A School Where Every Student Is Known

West Hollywood College Preparatory School is a private, nonprofit Pre‑school through 12th grade center of learning located in the heart of West Hollywood, California. We emphasize achievement in math, language arts, and science.

Students learn in a nurturing environment with small classes, enjoy a superb curriculum and faculty, and are encouraged to participate in civic and community life. Our intimate class sizes mean every student is seen, challenged, and supported — from their first day of pre‑school to their college acceptance letter.

Home/About/Principal’s Message

Principal’s Message

A personal welcome from the principal of West Hollywood College Preparatory School.

From the Principal

Welcome to WHCP

Welcome to West Hollywood College Preparatory School. Our school stands as a beacon of educational excellence in the heart of West Hollywood, providing students from Pre‑school through 12th grade with the tools, knowledge, and values they need to thrive in a rapidly changing world.

At WHCP, we believe that every child deserves a personalized education that honors their unique strengths and nurtures their curiosity. Our small class sizes are intentional. They allow our outstanding faculty to build genuine relationships with every student and tailor instruction to meet each learner where they are.

We place a special emphasis on math, language arts, and science. Our graduates consistently gain admission to top colleges and universities, and they carry with them not just academic preparation, but a deep sense of civic responsibility and community engagement.

I invite you to come visit our campus, meet our team, and see firsthand what makes WHCP such a special place to learn and grow. We are open for enrollment throughout the year and welcome families from all backgrounds.

— WHCP Principal

Home/About/Mission & Goals

Mission & Goals

The principles that guide every decision, every classroom, and every student’s journey at WHCP.

Our Mission
West Hollywood College Preparatory School is dedicated to preparing young minds for the future by providing an exceptional, personalized education in a nurturing environment that fosters academic excellence, civic responsibility, and lifelong learning.
What We Value

Four Commitments

Academic Excellence

We hold our students to the highest academic standards, with a rigorous curriculum that emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and a deep love of learning, especially in math and the sciences.

Personalized Learning

Small class sizes ensure that every student receives individualized attention. Our teachers know each student by name and tailor instruction to support their unique needs and aspirations.

Civic Engagement

We prepare students not just for college, but for life as engaged citizens. Students are encouraged to participate actively in the West Hollywood community and beyond.

Whole-Child Development

Academic success is only part of the picture. We nurture the emotional, social, and character development of every student, producing graduates who are thoughtful, compassionate, and resilient.

Strategic Goals

What We Strive For

1
College Readiness for Every Student

Ensure that every WHCP graduate is academically prepared and personally confident to succeed at a four-year university or the post-secondary path of their choice.

2
Academic Excellence

Maintain our reputation as a leader in math, language arts, and science education, preparing students for success in college and beyond.

3
An Inclusive, Welcoming Community

Foster a diverse, inclusive school environment where students from all backgrounds, including international students, feel welcomed, respected, and supported.

4
Family Partnership

Build strong partnerships with parents and families, keeping them informed, involved, and empowered as essential partners in their child’s education.

Home/Programs/Early Childhood

Early Childhood Education

Pre‑school & Kindergarten. Play-based, developmentally rich learning that sparks a lifelong love of discovery.

Licensed Childcare Center

Learning Through Play

WHCP’s Early Childhood Education program provides a safe, nurturing, and stimulating environment for our youngest learners in Pre‑school and Kindergarten. Our experienced early childhood educators understand child development deeply and design every activity to build both skills and joy.

We believe that play is the work of childhood. Through guided play, exploration, storytelling, music, and hands-on activities, our young students develop language, mathematical thinking, social skills, and creative expression, all while having fun.

Program Goals

  • Build language and early literacy foundations
  • Develop number sense and early math concepts
  • Foster curiosity, creativity, and a love of learning
  • Build social and emotional skills: sharing, empathy, cooperation
  • Prepare children seamlessly for Kindergarten and beyond

A Safe, Nurturing Space

Our early childhood classrooms are bright, welcoming, and designed with young learners in mind. We maintain very small group sizes so that every child receives individual attention and care. Our teachers are warm, patient, and deeply committed to each child’s development.

Ages Served

Pre‑school · Ages 2–4Kindergarten · Age 5

Program Features

Play-based learning
Very small group sizes
Experienced ECE staff
Social-emotional focus
Kindergarten-readiness preparation

Home/Programs/Elementary

Elementary School

Grades 1–5. Building the foundation for a lifetime of learning in a warm, nurturing environment.

A Strong Foundation

Our Elementary program gives students in grades 1–5 the strong academic and social foundations they need to thrive. Our talented, caring teachers create classrooms where every child feels safe, seen, and eager to learn.

We understand that the early elementary years are formative. That is why we invest so heavily in small class sizes and individualized instruction, so that every child’s needs are met, every curiosity is honored, and every student builds genuine confidence as a learner.

What We Teach

  • Reading, phonics, and writing foundations
  • Mathematics and early numeracy
  • Science exploration and inquiry
  • History and social studies
  • Arts, music, and physical education
  • Social-emotional learning and character development

The WHCP Difference

Elementary students at WHCP benefit from the same high standards and dedicated faculty that make our middle and high school program exceptional. As students progress, they are seamlessly prepared for the rigors of WHCP’s college-prep upper school curriculum.

Grade Levels

Home/Programs/Middle & High School

Middle & High School

Grades 6–12. A rigorous, college-preparatory education with a distinctive emphasis on math, language arts, and science.

College Preparatory Excellence

WHCP’s Middle and High School program is designed to challenge and inspire students in grades 6 through 12. Our college-preparatory curriculum is built on high academic standards, small class sizes, and a faculty that genuinely cares about every student’s success.

We place a particular emphasis on math, language arts, and science. Our students regularly advance well beyond grade level, giving them a significant advantage when applying to top universities.

Curriculum Highlights

  • Advanced mathematics through Calculus and beyond
  • Physics, Chemistry, and Biology with hands-on lab work
  • English Language Arts and Composition
  • History, Government, and Social Sciences
  • Foreign languages
  • College application counseling beginning in 10th grade
  • SAT/ACT preparation integrated into the curriculum

Small Classes, Personal Attention

Our middle and high school classes are kept intentionally small. Every student is known by their teachers, learning is personalized, expectations are high, and the results speak for themselves.

Grade Levels

Grade 6Grade 7Grade 8Grade 9Grade 10Grade 11Grade 12

After school childcare and enrichment — a safe and engaging space for students beyond the school day.

After School Care

WHCP’s After School program provides working families with reliable, high-quality care after the regular school day. Our program is staffed by caring WHCP educators who know the students, ensure safety, and make the extended day both productive and enjoyable.

Home/Programs/Individual Programs

Individual Programs

Fully customized, one-on-one learning designed around each student’s unique needs, goals, and pace.

Learning Built Around You

WHCP’s Individual Programs offer a completely personalized educational experience for students who need or prefer a one-on-one learning environment. Whether a student needs remedial support, is academically accelerated, or has unique learning needs, we build a custom program around them.

Who Benefits

  • Students needing to catch up in specific subjects
  • Advanced students ready to move beyond grade level
  • Students with learning differences who thrive one-on-one
  • Students recovering from illness or extended absence
  • Home-school students seeking structured supplemental instruction
  • Students preparing for high-stakes exams

How It Works

Each individual program begins with an assessment to understand the student’s current level, learning style, and goals. We then design a custom curriculum, set benchmarks, and pair the student with the teacher who is the best match. Progress is reviewed regularly and the program adjusts as needed.

Program Features

100% personalized
Flexible scheduling
All subjects available
Regular progress reviews
All ages welcome
Pricing varies by program

Get Started

Contact us for an initial consultation. We will discuss your student’s needs and design the right program.

Home/Programs/Tutoring

Tutoring Center

Expert subject tutoring for students of all ages and grade levels, with flexible scheduling to fit your family.

Expert Academic Support

WHCP’s Tutoring Center provides targeted, expert academic support in all core subjects. Our tutors are professional, experienced subject-matter specialists who know how to identify gaps, build understanding, and restore student confidence.

Whether a student is struggling with a single concept or needs ongoing support in a subject, our tutors deliver clear, patient, and effective instruction at the student’s pace.

Subjects We Cover

  • Mathematics (all levels, through Calculus)
  • Physics, Chemistry, Biology
  • English Language Arts and writing
  • History and social studies
  • Foreign languages
  • SAT, ACT, and standardized test preparation
  • Study skills and academic organization

Flexible Scheduling

We offer tutoring sessions after school, on weekends, and during school breaks. Sessions can be scheduled as needed or as recurring appointments. We work with your family’s schedule to make tutoring accessible and consistent.

Session Options

One-on-one sessions
Small group (2–3 students)
Intensive test prep packages

Home/Programs/International Students

International Students

A welcoming home for students from around the world, with the dedicated support needed to thrive in U.S. education.

A Home Away From Home

WHCP proudly welcomes students from countries around the world. Our International Student Program provides the specialized support, resources, and community that international students need to succeed academically and feel at home in West Hollywood.

We understand that transitioning to a new country, language, and school system is challenging. Our dedicated international student coordinator works closely with each student and their family to ensure a smooth transition and ongoing success.

Program Support

  • English as a Second Language (ESL) instruction
  • Academic support and subject tutoring
  • Cultural orientation and adjustment support
  • I-20 and student visa documentation assistance
  • Family communication support
  • Housing referral resources, if needed
  • Integration into the broader WHCP community

Los Angeles & West Hollywood

Students who attend WHCP get to experience life in one of the world’s most vibrant, diverse cities. West Hollywood is a welcoming, culturally rich neighborhood and a wonderful home base for an international student’s American experience.

We Serve

Students in Grades K–12, from any country, are welcome.

We Offer

ESL instruction
I-20 documentation
Cultural support
Dedicated coordinator
Family communication

We accept international students year-round. Contact us to begin the application process.

Home/Students

Student Life

Activities, leadership, community service, and academic support for every WHCP student.

Enrichment

Student Activities

Students are encouraged to participate in after-school and extracurricular activities for their own enrichment and to strengthen their college applications. Schoolwork always comes first — activities are supported by a faculty or parent advisor once enough students express interest.

Activities Available

Depending on student interest, activities may include Student Government, class trips, school fundraisers, local election campaigns, the Student Art Show, and Chess.

Field Trips

Educational trips supplement classroom learning several times per year. Students and parents may suggest and help plan trips. Past destinations include the Natural History Museum, the Getty Center, the Skirball Cultural Center, West Hollywood City Hall, the Museum of Latin American Art, and theater outings.

Leadership

Student Government

Middle and High School students in grades 6–12 can serve as student body leaders in WHCP's Student Government, hosting activities and fundraisers throughout the year under a faculty advisor.

Past activities include a bake sale for Breast Cancer Awareness, the Halloween Potluck Party, the Thanksgiving Celebration & Show, and a bake sale benefiting the Lange Foundation animal shelter.

Giving Back

Community Service

WHCP requires students in grades 9–12 to complete 100 community service hours prior to graduation. Counselors and staff help identify opportunities suited to each student's interests and abilities, and keep records of participation. Parental support is essential.

Past Projects

West Hollywood Book Fair · Revlon Walk for Breast Cancer · AIDS Walk Los Angeles · West Hollywood Kids Fair · West Hollywood Russian Culture Festival · West Hollywood Holocaust Remembrance Day · Red Cross Hurricane Katrina Relief Fund.

Support

Academic Counseling

In WHCP's small school setting, teachers, counselors, and administrators team up to motivate students and help them be their best — academically, personally, and socially. We promote responsibility, self-discipline, strong ethics, and self-respect alongside rigorous college preparation.

Registration & Planning

Students are registered in classes based on ability and achievement, and assisted in building a long-range academic plan that prepares them for future training and work.

Home/Parents

Parent Resources

Information and opportunities for parents to stay engaged and involved in the WHCP community.

Get Involved

Parent Involvement

Parent involvement is essential to the success of students at WHCP. Parents are encouraged to take part in school life in a number of ways:

PTO Meetings

Participate in monthly Parent Teacher Organization meetings. The PTO helps organize school events and projects, leads fundraisers, and coordinates parents and teachers in these activities.

Field Trips

Assist with school field trips by driving children to destinations and acting as chaperones throughout the year.

Progress Meetings

Request student progress report meetings, available throughout the year, where parents meet with teachers to discuss their child's academic development.

Events & Projects

Participate in school projects and events throughout the year — helping organize, supplying resources, and attending are all great ways to be part of student life.

Activity Advisor

Become an advisor for after-school student activities such as Student Government, the Student Art Show, and school fundraisers, based on student interest.

Career Day

Come share what you do for work with our students at Career Day, helping them learn about different careers and pathways.

PTO

Parent Teacher Organization

WHCP's Parent Teacher Organization meets regularly to discuss ways for parents to enhance the quality of, and resources for, student life and learning. We invite you to become a PTO leader — organizing school projects, events, and fundraisers and bringing other parents and teachers on board to support your work.

To attend our next PTO meeting, please contact the school office.

Contact the School Office
Communication

Parent & Teacher Meetings

We encourage parents and teachers to communicate about their child's progress throughout the school year. Healthy parent–teacher partnerships are key to every student's success.

Meetings by Request

Parents may request a meeting with a teacher at any time through the Director. Teachers may also request meetings with parents, and families will be notified by the Director.

Privacy Policy

How West Hollywood College Preparatory School collects, uses, and protects your information.

Effective date: January 1, 2026

West Hollywood College Preparatory School (“WHCP,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) respects your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains what information we collect through this website, how we use it, and the choices you have. It applies to information collected through this site and is provided in keeping with the California Online Privacy Protection Act (CalOPPA) and other applicable privacy laws.

Information We Collect

We collect personal information only when you choose to provide it — primarily through our contact and admissions inquiry forms. Depending on the form, the categories of personally identifiable information we may collect include:

  • Identifiers such as your name and, for admissions inquiries, a prospective student’s name;
  • Contact details such as email address and telephone number;
  • The program of interest and any message or comments you submit; and
  • Limited technical information your browser sends automatically, such as general device or browser type.

We do not knowingly collect payment card numbers, government identification numbers, or sensitive personal information through this website.

How We Use Your Information

We use the information you provide to respond to your inquiry, process admissions interest, schedule tours, communicate with you about our programs, and improve our services. We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it with third parties for their own marketing purposes.

Categories of Third Parties

We may share information with service providers who help us operate this website and respond to inquiries — for example, our form-processing and email-delivery provider, and our website hosting provider. These providers act on our behalf and are not authorized to use your information for unrelated purposes. We may also disclose information when required by law or to protect the rights and safety of our community.

Cookies & Do Not Track

This website does not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies, and we do not track visitors across other websites over time. Because we do not track you across third-party websites, we do not respond differently to “Do Not Track” (DNT) signals sent by your browser. We are not aware of third parties collecting personally identifiable information about your online activities across different websites when you visit this site.

Student & Children’s Privacy

Inquiry forms on this site are intended to be completed by parents, guardians, or prospective adult students. We are committed to protecting the privacy of children and students and handle any student information consistent with applicable laws, including the federal Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and California student-privacy laws. Please do not submit a child’s information through this site except as part of a parent- or guardian-initiated admissions inquiry.

How We Protect Your Information

We maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect the information submitted through this website. No method of transmission over the Internet is completely secure, however, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

Reviewing or Changing Your Information

You may request to review, update, or delete the personal information you have submitted through this website by contacting us using the details below. We will respond to your request consistent with applicable law.

Your California Privacy Rights

California residents may have rights regarding their personal information under California law. To exercise any available rights, or to ask how your information is handled, please contact us using the information below.

Changes to This Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. When we make material changes, we will revise the effective date above and post the updated policy on this page. We encourage you to review it periodically.

Contact Us

If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or our privacy practices, contact us at:

West Hollywood College Preparatory School
1317 N. Crescent Heights Blvd., West Hollywood, CA 90046
Telephone: (323) 822-7900

Home/Terms of Use

Terms of Use

The terms governing your use of the WHCP website.

Effective date: January 1, 2026

Welcome to the West Hollywood College Preparatory School website. By accessing or using this website, you agree to these Terms of Use. If you do not agree, please do not use the site.

Use of This Website

This website is provided for general informational purposes about WHCP and its programs. You agree to use it only for lawful purposes and not to interfere with its operation or attempt to access it in any unauthorized manner.

Accuracy of Information

We strive to keep the information on this site accurate and current, including details about programs, tuition, and events. However, information is provided “as is” and may change without notice. Tuition figures, schedules, and program details should be confirmed with the school’s admissions office before you rely on them.

Website Design & AI-Assisted Content

Accessibility Statement

Our commitment to making this website usable for everyone.

Effective date: January 1, 2026

West Hollywood College Preparatory School is committed to ensuring that our website is accessible to people with disabilities, and to providing full and equal access to the information and services we offer online.

Our Standard

We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA, the standard widely recognized under the Americans with Disabilities Act and the California Unruh Civil Rights Act. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible to people with a wide range of disabilities.

Measures We Take

  • Descriptive text alternatives for meaningful images;
  • Clear, consistent navigation and a “skip to main content” link for keyboard users;
  • Labeled form fields and clear error and confirmation messages;
  • Visible keyboard focus indicators and full keyboard operability;
  • Readable text, structured headings, and support for reduced-motion preferences.

Ongoing Effort

Accessibility is an ongoing effort. We continue to review and improve the site, and we recognize that some content may not yet fully meet our target standard. We welcome your feedback to help us identify and resolve any barriers.
